title: Hatchling pens — Nile crocodiles: sudden deaths with swollen joints
presentation: A crocodile farm reports fourteen deaths among 400 hatchlings over ten days. Affected animals are lethargic, float oddly, and several have swollen limb joints. Water quality has been unstable since a filter failure.

stages.title: Assess the group and the environment
stages.briefing: Affected hatchlings: lethargic, buoyant and listing in the water, reluctant to feed, several with swollen carpal and tarsal joints, some with pale gum margins and petechiae on the ventral scales. Water: temperature 26°C (target 30–32°C), ammonia 0.8 mg/L, nitrite 0.4 mg/L, heavy organic load, filter failed eleven days ago. Stocking density recently increased.
stages.prompt: Which findings suggest systemic bacterial disease?

options.label: Swollen joints in several animals with ventral petechiae
options.detail: Haematogenous spread with vasculitis

options.label: Fourteen deaths in ten days after a filter failure
options.detail: An environmental insult followed by an outbreak

options.label: Abnormal buoyancy with listing
options.detail: Coelomic or pulmonary involvement

options.label: Water temperature 26°C
options.detail: Immunosuppressive, and the reason rather than the sign

options.label: Reluctance to feed
options.detail: Universal in sick reptiles

stages.explanation: Polyarthritis with petechiae across a group is septicaemia, not an injury, and the timeline pins it to the filter failure eleven days ago. Cold, ammonia-laden water suppresses reptile immunity within days, which is why the environmental readings are part of the diagnosis rather than background detail.

stages.title: Choose the samples
stages.briefing: Fresh carcasses are available and you can sample live animals and the water.

options.label: Post-mortem with bacterial culture of liver, joint fluid and blood
options.detail: Confirms septicaemia and names the organism

options.label: Antibiotic sensitivity testing on the isolates
options.detail: Aquatic Gram-negatives are frequently resistant

options.label: Joint fluid cytology from affected hatchlings
options.detail: Septic versus non-septic arthritis

options.label: Full water quality analysis — ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, temperature, organic load
options.detail: The driver, measured properly

options.label: Histopathology of liver, lung, kidney and joints
options.detail: Distribution of lesions and chronicity

options.label: Serology for West Nile virus as the primary test
options.detail: A real crocodilian pathogen, but not what a filter failure and polyarthritis point to first

options.label: Skin scrapes for ectoparasites
options.detail: Will not explain deaths with swollen joints

stages.explanation: Culture from more than one site is what separates a true septicaemia from post-mortem contamination — liver, joint and blood agreeing is convincing. Sensitivity testing matters because these are Aeromonas and Salmonella-type organisms with unpredictable resistance. Water analysis is a diagnostic test here, not a compliance exercise.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Culture: Aeromonas hydrophila from liver, blood and joint fluid in four of five hatchlings; Salmonella species also isolated from two intestines. Sensitivity: resistant to amoxicillin, sensitive to trimethoprim-sulfonamide and to ceftazidime. Joint fluid cytology: heterophilic inflammation with intracellular bacteria. Histopathology: multifocal hepatic necrosis, fibrinous arthritis, renal tubular necrosis. Water: ammonia 0.8 mg/L, nitrite 0.4 mg/L, temperature 26°C. West Nile virus not tested.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Aeromonas hydrophila septicaemia with fibrinous polyarthritis
options.detail: The same organism from three sites with matching lesions

options.label: Poor water quality and low temperature precipitated the outbreak
options.detail: Ammonia and nitrite raised, water 4–6°C below target

options.label: Treatment must follow sensitivity results
options.detail: Resistant to amoxicillin

options.label: Salmonella carriage is a zoonotic risk for staff
options.detail: Isolated from intestines — a handling and hygiene issue

options.label: West Nile virus has been excluded
options.detail: It was not tested; it is unlikely, not excluded

options.label: Trauma from increased stocking density is the primary cause
options.detail: Density is a stressor; the lesions are infectious

stages.explanation: One organism from liver, blood and joint fluid, with fibrin in the joints on histology, is as clean a septicaemia diagnosis as farm material allows. Being precise about the untested virus matters: "unlikely" and "excluded" are different claims, and only one of them is honest here. The Salmonella finding changes what staff are told about gloves and hand hygiene.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Aeromonas hydrophila from liver, blood and joint fluid, heterophilic joint inflammation with intracellular bacteria, hepatic and renal necrosis, ammonia 0.8 mg/L with nitrite 0.4 mg/L at 26°C, incidental Salmonella carriage.

options.label: Aeromonas septicaemia with polyarthritis, precipitated by water quality failure and low temperature
options.detail: Agent, lesions and the environmental cause

options.label: Primary salmonellosis
options.detail: Isolated from gut only, not from the systemic sites

options.label: West Nile virus infection
options.detail: Not tested and not supported by these lesions

options.label: Nutritional myopathy
options.detail: Would not produce fibrinous arthritis or positive blood cultures

options.label: Traumatic joint injury from overstocking
options.detail: Cytology and culture show sepsis

stages.explanation: The diagnosis has to name the water, because that is what stops the outbreak: filtration restored, temperature back to 30–32°C, stocking density reduced and the organic load cleared, alongside a sensitivity-guided antibiotic for affected hatchlings. Treating crocodiles in bad water is how a farm loses a whole cohort.
